title: Introduce latency-distribution-collector and histogram-exporter for perf runs
author: Priya Kaur
commits: a1d3f4c: add initial latency_collector prototype and unit tests
b2c5e7a: implement fixed-window histogram exporter and Prometheus aggregation hook
c7f8aa2: wire collector into CI perf pipeline and add example script
d3b9f55: docs: add usage and validation guide for latency distribution outputs
e5a1b20: tests: expand to edge cases for variable sequence lengths
description: Motivation: our current perf suite reports mean/median p50/p95/p99 but lacks a first-class histogram distribution export that lets ops and product slices examine tail behavior by bucket and request class. This PR introduces a latency-distribution-collector (benchmarks/runner/latency_collector.py) and a histogram_exporter that emits fixed-window histograms and a Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint for aggregated CI runs. Key changes: 1) adds a thread-safe latency_collector that supports labeled buckets (model, route, sequence_length_bin) and controlled flush intervals; 2) implements histogram_exporter with configurable bucket boundaries and JSON/Prometheus output modes; 3) integrates collection step into ci/perf-pipeline.yml so nightly jobs persist artifacts to the perf artifacts store; 4) adds validation tests and an examples script to reproduce locally. Implementation notes: the collector uses a ring buffer to bound memory and an optimized bucket increment path to minimize overhead during tight throughput tests; the exporter supports on-the-fly delta exports to reduce payload size for long runs. Checklist: - [x] design and prototype latency collector; - [x] unit tests covering concurrency and bucket edge cases; - [x] exporter with both JSON and Prometheus formats; - [x] CI integration and artifact upload; - [x] docs and example runbook. Backwards compatibility: output formats default to JSON with the old summary generator still available; no changes to existing benchmark input schemas. Perf: measured <1% overhead at 2k rps in synthetic harness; added ability to capture per-route tail behavior that was previously invisible. How to validate: run examples/bench/collect_and_export.sh against a local runner to produce artifacts and then run docs/benchmarks/latency-distribution.md validation steps which include checksum and bucket-sanity assertions. Related work: follows on ENG-4012 (tail-analysis initiative) and pairs with the perf-viewer dashboard from ENG-3987. Security: exporter binds only to loopback by default and CI uploads go to the internal artifacts bucket with ACLs. Release notes: Adds latency distribution collector and histogram exporter to benchmark lab enabling tail analysis and Prometheus-compatible exports. Breaking change: false.
